name: NAOMS-Rust
purpose: A clean-room Rust rebuild of the NAOMS core as reusable crates, written spec-first, to replace the TypeScript daemon.

stack.didMethods: did:key root; did:naoms for chains and hives; did:peer (numalgo 2/4); did:webvh, never required to resolve
stack.credentials: W3C VC 2.0 with a DataIntegrityProof (eddsa-jcs-2022); own Naoms* credential family
stack.transport: Any protocol over any network: native TSP 1.0, DIDComm v2, iroh/QUIC, WebRTC, Reticulum, Nostr, BLE and HTTPS, each written from the spec
stack.groups: Hives as signed hash chains with a quorum from current membership; Authority credentials for roles
stack.devices: FROST threshold signing across a person's devices (keyholder crate); did:key as root

credentials.note: Spec-first redesign, five credential kinds: Relationship (VRC); Authority forms Membership (VMC), Role and Permission (VAC), Delegation (VDC); Attribute (VSC); Opinion (vouch) and Achievement (project, thanks, service) both carry an endorsement (VEC). Core code not public.

replication.note: Chain crate written from the spec. Code not public.

requiredParty: a steward, per the public material

did-resolution.note: Four DID methods specified (did:key, did:naoms, did:peer, did:webvh); did:webvh is never required to resolve. No public resolver yet.

shared-room.note: Hives as signed hash chains with a membership quorum.

multi-device.note: FROST threshold signing in the keyholder crate.

captured-device.note: Recovery after a lost or captured device: FROST threshold signing (keyholder crate) so a single seized device holds no usable key, plus social-recovery buddies to re-establish a new device. Specified; no public code or vectors yet. Describes recovery; removing the device and rotating the group key are not described yet.

document-framework.note: A plugin and package host (a WIT world), not the Trust Tasks Framework.
